title: Signed dual-complex scalar calculus, towers and localization
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $P$ a bounded cochain complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Put $P_S=P\otimes_R S$ termwise [def-weil-module-base-change], and $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$, with $d(f)=-(-1)^j f d_P$ for homogeneous $f$ of degree $j$, using the one-object ringed-site version of [def-pur-hom-complex]. Order evaluation as $P\otimes P^\vee\to R[0]$, with value $(-1)^{pj}f(x)$ on $x\in P^p$ and $f\in(P^\vee)^j$ (zero unless $p+j=0$).
The balanced formula
$$\beta_{S/R,P}(f\otimes a)(x\otimes b)=\iota(f(x))ab$$
defines an $S$-linear isomorphism of cochain complexes $P^\vee\otimes_R S\to\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(P_S,S[0])$. In this formula $\iota:R\to S$ is the given map. It obeys $d\beta(f\otimes a)=\beta(df\otimes a)$ and intertwines signed evaluation with scalar extension: both uncurried evaluations on $(x\otimes b)\otimes(f\otimes a)$ are $(-1)^{pj}\iota(f(x))ab$. The terms of $P_S$ and of its dual are finite projective. These maps define a natural transformation on the perfect derived category $\operatorname{Perf}(R)\subset D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], independent of the chosen bounded finite-projective representative. For a derived morphism $u:P\to Q$, contravariance is precomposition, and
$$\beta_{S/R,P}(u^\vee\otimes1)=(u\otimes1)^\vee\beta_{S/R,Q}.$$
For $S=R$, $\beta$ is the identity under multiplication. For a further ring homomorphism $S\to T$, successive $\beta$ maps and the direct $R\to T$ map agree through the balanced associators $(z\otimes a)\otimes c\mapsto z\otimes\iota_{S,T}(a)c$. On the successive arguments $((f\otimes a)\otimes c)$ and $((x\otimes b)\otimes d)$ both dual maps give $\iota_{R,T}(f(x))\iota_{S,T}(ab)cd$.
For any multiplicative subset $U\subset R$, termwise localization $U^{-1}(-)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and the canonical dual identification for $U^{-1}P$ is $\beta_{U^{-1}R/R,P}$. Localizing any of the preceding maps and equations gives the same maps and equations over the localized rings, including their signed evaluation, naturality and tower equations.

proof.text: Identify degree j of the recorded Hom complex into R[0] with the ordinary module dual of degree -j using Cochain.toSingleEquiv. Mathlib Module.dual_projective and Module.dual_finite give finite projectivity of each dual term. Tensor-product projectivity and finiteness instances give finite projectivity of scalar-extended terms. The ordinary dual/scalar equivalence is TensorProduct.comm followed by dualTensorHomEquiv and the extension/restriction-of-scalars adjunction; its pure-tensor formula identifies it with beta degreewise.

proof.text: Construct scalarCochain by applying extension of scalars to each cochain component and composing with the coefficient-unit comparison. Its R-linearity follows from scalar compatibility of extension. The extension/restriction adjunction gives betaX. The Hom differential identities for functorial maps and postcomposition prove commutation with differentials, giving beta. Evaluating the adjunction on pure tensors gives f(z(x))*a*b.

Identify each degree with an ordinary dual by HomComplex.Cochain.toSingleEquiv. The composite of TensorProduct.comm, dualTensorHomEquiv and the additive scalar adjunction is bijective. Its pure-tensor formula agrees with betaX, so betaX is bijective and beta is an isomorphism. Mathlib module dual and tensor-product instances prove every claimed finite-projectivity clause.

proof.text: The chain-map compatibility for beta follows directly from HomComplex.δ_map and HomComplex.δ_comp_ofHom. Precomposition is composition by the degree-zero cocycle of a chain map; HomComplex.δ_ofHom_comp verifies its differential equation.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), differential formula specialized to R[0].

proof.text: Use the signed evaluation given by [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model]. On every direct-sum tensor summand compare pure tensors. The scalar tensorator multiplies the two scalar factors. Both paths evaluate to (-1)^(p*j)*f(z(x))*a*b. Outside total degree zero the coefficient complex is zero. In degree zero the beta pure-tensor formula and additive compatibility with the sign prove equality.

source.place: Tag 0FNG (section-sign-rules), tensor differential and Koszul symmetry; explicit signed evaluation calculation.

proof.text: Define precomposition by composition with the degree-zero cocycle of a chain map in the product Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]. HomComplex differential composition identities show it is a chain map. Comparing cochain components proves beta naturality, identity and tower equations directly, with scalar multiplication associativity and commutativity on pure tensors. No passage to homotopy classes is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A8H (section-hom-complexes): explicit dual homotopy calculation for the signed differential.

proof.text: Apply the proved canonical derived comparison [lem-pod-perfect-dual-derived-transport] to the concrete beta maps, the signed evaluation supplied by [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model], the proved chain evaluation square and finite-projective term assertions, and DerivedCategory.IsPerfect.ihom_unit. The result supplies derived naturality, model compatibility, evaluation, identity and tower equations.

Evaluate the identity and tower equations for beta on scalar pure tensors. The identity extension multiplies scalars; for R → S → T both paths give g(f(z(x))) * g(a*b) * c*d. The tensor universal property proves equality of the chain maps. The derived identity and tower equations are obtained separately from the canonical comparison theorem in step 7.

source.place: Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product); balanced tower and identity calculations, with the derived comparison from the cited node.

proof.text: The existing localization functor is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Its map on complexes therefore preserves quasi-isomorphisms by the Mathlib exact-functor API, for arbitrary complexes and multiplicative subsets.

source.place: Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact); elementary cycles, boundaries and quotient calculation.

proof.text: Use the base-change universal property of the localization map to identify A ⊗_R M with U^{-1}M for A=U^{-1}R. Tensor balancing and the localization universal property prove naturality. Its inverse sends x/t to (1/t) tensor x. Conjugate beta by this natural isomorphism and precompose by its inverse on the original complex. The beta coordinate formula and multiplication of localized fractions give z(x)/(s*t). The same proof includes the zero ring and multiplicative subsets containing zero.

source.place: Sections 00CM (section-localization) and 00CV (section-tensor-product); explicit fraction and tower formulas.
